speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, working mothers with a monthly household income of $12,000 or below are eligible for a means-tested Additional Subsidy, with lower income families receiving higher subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Families with Singaporean children enrolled in kindergartens run by Anchor Operators and MOE and whose monthly household income is $12,000 or below are eligible for a means-tested subsidy under the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme or KiFAS.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Larger families can choose to have their household income assessed on a per capita basis, which may enable them to qualify for a higher tier of the Additional Subsidy or KiFAS.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, 103,400 Singaporean children are enrolled in full-day childcare.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Of these, all receive a Basic Subsidy each month.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Sixty-one thousand five hundred children, or six in 10, receive an Additional Subsidy each month, as their families have monthly household income of $12,000 or below.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Nine thousand nine hundred children, or one in 10, receive the highest tier of the Additional Subsidy, as they are from families with monthly household income of $3,000 and below.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For kindergarten, 18,800 Singaporean children are enrolled in Anchor Operator- and MOE-run kindergartens.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Of these, 12,000 children, or over six in 10, receive KiFAS each month, as their families have monthly household income of $12,000 or below.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For this group, the median subsidy is $156 and the median nett fee after subsidy is $15.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Four thousand three hundred children, or two in 10, receive the highest tier of the KiFAS subsidy, as their families have monthly household income of $3,000 or below.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For this group, the median subsidy is $170 and the nett fee is $1.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Member asked if we could extend subsidies to non-working mothers taking care of older children in the family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Non-working mothers who need childcare due to certain circumstances, such as those who are looking for employment or are caring for a younger child aged 24 months and below, a special needs child or a sick family member, can apply for the same subsidies as working mothers under Special Approval.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: From August 2020, families under HDB's Public Rental Scheme and MSF’s ComCare schemes automatically qualify for maximum pre-school subsidies, regardless of the mother’s working status.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Non-working mothers may also consider enrolling their children in half-day kindergarten programmes, which are often more affordable than full-day childcare programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: KiFAS is available at kindergartens run by Anchor Operators and MOE, and does not depend on the mother's working status.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As for student care, student care centres provide care and supervision to school-going children from seven to 14 years old.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To ensure that student care remains affordable, MSF provides children from lower income families with monthly subsidies for student care fees under the Student Care Fee Assistance or SCFA scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These subsidies are available for all eligible families with monthly household income of $4,500 or below or per capita income of $1,125 or below, including those with non-working parents who are looking for work, on medical leave, or with certified full-time care-giver duties for a dependant and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Around 36,000 children are enrolled in MSF-registered student care centres today, of which 6,600 Singaporean children are SCFA beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Of the 6,600 children, the median SCFA subsidy is $243, and the median net fee after subsidy is $30.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One thousand and eight hundred children, or three in 10, receive the highest tier of the SCFA subsidy, as their families have monthly household income of $1,500 and below.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The median SCFA subsidy is $275 and the median net fee after subsidy is $5.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Thirty five percent of these 1,800 children have zero household income.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Member also asked if we could eliminate means-testing so that families can pay a uniform fee for pre-school and student care.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Means-testing allows the Government to use fiscal resources more effectively and to extend more support to families with greater needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We also increased the subsidy amounts for each eligible tier, by up to $240 per month for the Additional Subsidy.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Similarly, for student care, we recently enhanced the SCFA scheme to strengthen support for lower income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In July 2020, the monthly household income ceiling was raised from $4,000 to $4,500.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The per capita income ceiling was raised from $1,000 to $1,125, allowing more families to qualify for subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The quanta for means-tested SCFA subsidies have also been increased, such that eligible families can receive up to $60 more in subsidies per month.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will monitor the impact of the enhancements, because these are very recent, and review these schemes when necessary to ensure the affordability of pre-school and student care, especially for lower income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For pre-school, we aim to lower fee caps for full-day childcare at Government-supported pre-schools over the medium term to make pre-school even more affordable for all families, starting with Partner Operator pre-schools in January 2021.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, I appreciate all the effort that is given by the Government to the families.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This means, based on the number of children they have, they have more subsidy, higher quantum given to them.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is also to ease the burden, especially faced by the sandwiched class and encouraging them to have more babies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For childcare, for example, we want to make sure that children get access to affordable and quality pre-school education.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That is very important, especially during the growing years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So if Members know of families who do not qualify because of this income criteria, they can always come forward and appeal for higher subsidies.
